_comment: The canonical A11 serialization tags, once, for every language.
A tag is what identifies a type on the wire: the `type` parameter of a
chunk's MIME type. It is the only place a type is ever named -- nothing
inside a payload repeats it, and a value the format already describes
(an object, an array, a string) carries no tag at all. Each language
kotlin/src/main/kotlin/a11/SerialTags.kt) and asserts them against this
file in its test suite, so a tag renamed in one language and forgotten in
another fails a test instead of a conversation.
Keys are language-neutral names for the concept; values are the wire tags.
`media_types` is the other half of the same contract: which media type each
language uses for the values whose type the media type itself describes.
text/plain is UTF-8 text and application/octet-stream is bytes, and a chunk
using either carries no `type` parameter and no framing inside the payload --
the bytes on the wire are the value. Those two are the defaults for a string
